governance.attested_by: ercot 27 ordc-structure-v1: ercot 26 gtc-limits base + ORDC-era 2023 price-formation structure (WS1/WS2), 2026-07-03
governance.note: ercot 27 = ercot 26 gtc-limits recipe + three structural mechanisms, no offer-curve retuning and zero parameters fitted to a price or volume residual. (1) Multi-product AS co-opt with COMMITMENT-STATE-AWARE reserve headroom (WS1): ercot_multiproduct_as_coopt + ercot_as_aware_commitment run the AS-aware P2 screen (energy + AS revenue from the model's OWN P1 reserve duals; AS-adequacy floor at the MEASURED ASPLANNP433 requirement, frac 1.0), and the P2 co-opt draws reserve on that commitment state instead of all-online availability: decommitted slow-start capacity leaves the shared-headroom RHS including its econ/peak tranches (couple_peak - a cold plant's duct-firing band can neither generate nor hold reserve), online CTs join the synchronized (fast) pool per-hour via the P2 availability, and offline quick-start capacity backs Non-Spin only via a reserve-only extra-cap RHS (reserve_config.ercot_commitment_headroom_overrides). All commitment inputs are the solve's own economics plus physical start-capability classes - forward-regenerable, no measured series. (2) Published pre-reform ECRS deployment design (WS2, ercot_ecrs_conservative_deployment): from ECRS go-live (2023-06-10, M-D050523-01; onset carried by the ASPLANNP433 data) through 2024-07-31 ERCOT had NO price-based ECRS release to SCED (manual reliability deployment only; IMM 2023 SOM II.G: 'artificial shortage pricing ... doubled average energy prices between June and December 2023', >$12B), represented as a single ECRS demand step AT THE OFFER CAP so the withheld ~2 GW raises the energy dual endogenously; from 2024-08-01 (operating-procedure release trigger - the PUCT REJECTED NPRR1224's $750 floor on 2024-07-25, so no administrative release price exists) the family reverts to the standing VOLL-anchored ramp. Research correction recorded: the handoff's recalled '$2,000 ECRS proxy floor' does NOT exist in any primary source and is not modeled. (3) Endogenous storage energy-vs-AS split (G5, ercot_storage_as_endogenous). Measured RTORDPA and DAM-AS overlays kept ON with per-column persistence; the one-event-one-channel audit finds trivial overlap with the endogenous co-opt scarcity (2023 RTORDPA min-overlap ~$0.2k; 2024 DAM-AS ~$3.9k over 5 shared hours), so no double-counting channel is active. PROBE RESULT (registered, not promoted): the mechanisms move 2023's scarcity months toward actual (Jun residual -23.5 -> -12.9, Jul -10.1 -> -9.1, Oct/Nov ~0) but two structural defects dominate elsewhere and are ROOT-CAUSED, not tuned around: (a) the exact-coverage AS-adequacy floor (committed capacity ~= energy + AS requirement) leaves ~1.0x online-reserve coverage where ERCOT's measured RTOLCAP shows ~2x, so the shared-headroom dual elevates ALL months (Feb-2023 +$42.5 with ECRS not yet live isolates the artifact to the floor, not the ECRS design; 2024 +13.4%, 2025 +8.9% annual); (b) replacing the lumped co-opt product dropped the ORDC total-reserve demand curve - the actual published RTORPA mechanism of 2023-25 - so the deep 2023 tail collapses (Aug $101.5 vs keeper $145.6 vs actual $191.7; >$1000 tail 28 h vs 61 actual) while withholding alone lengthens the moderate tail (280 h > $200 vs 181). The structurally complete pre-RTC+B stack is BOTH product withholding AND the ORDC total-reserve curve, plus a commitment representation with realistic (~2x) online surplus - the documented follow-up. Keeper remains ercot 26 gtc-limits.
